Visited Foo, Andheri for a Pan-Asian meal at lunch time . The ambience is definitely one of the highlights — stylish interiors, good lighting, and a lively vibe that works well but still did not find it something out of the box or extraordinary.

The menu has a wide variety of Asian dishes, which is impressive, and the presentation of the food is However okayish for me. At best the food was 6/10 for me.

However, the overall experience was a bit inconsistent. Some dishes tasted good while others felt average for the price point. Portion sizes also felt very small considering the cost.i mean 4 pcs for an 800₹ sushi is too much.
Service was polite but slow at times, and we had to wait longer than expected for a few items.

Overall, it’s a decent place for ambience and variety, but the food has to be more consistent to fully justify the pricing. An okay experience, but there’s room for improvement.

For me , personally this is not a must visit place.

I had the misfortune of dining at The Grand Asian cuisine , and let me just say, this was an experience I'd rather forget. The name should have been a warning, but I foolishly ignored it.

The first red flag was the smell when I walked in—a rancid blend of burnt oil and something that could only be described as old gym socks. The decor looked like it hadn't been updated since the 70s, and not in a charming, retro way—more like they just never bothered.

I ordered the "special of the day," which was a mistake I'll regret forever. The steak was so overcooked it could have doubled as a hockey puck. It was dry, tasteless, and somehow both burnt and raw at the same time. The mashed potatoes on the side had the consistency of paste and the flavor of cardboard. The vegetables were a sad, mushy mess, as if they’d been boiled into oblivion.

And don't even get me started on the service. The waiter seemed more interested in his phone than in actually serving customers. When he did acknowledge my existence, it was with a look that said he had better things to do.

To top it all off, I ended the night with a stomach ache that left me questioning every decision that led me to this point. If you’re considering eating here, do yourself a favor and go literally anywhere else. Your stomach and taste buds will thank you.

That should capture the essence of a terrible food experience!

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dining at Baoji has, over the years, become more than just a meal for us—it’s a cherished ritual and a celebration of Pan-Asian excellence. Chef Kapil’s menu is nothing short of extraordinary—an immersive gastronomic journey across Asia where every dish is crafted with finesse, depth, and bold, unforgettable flavours. From the fragrant warmth of Thai curries to the delicate precision of Japanese classics, each plate feels thoughtfully curated and beautifully executed.

Over the years, we’ve explored almost every vegetarian and non-vegetarian offering on the menu, and the consistency is remarkable. Our all-time favourites include the Prawns Tempura Sushi, Spicy Crispy Prawns Cheung Fun, KRA Paw Rice, and the Spicy Teriyaki Chicken with Japanese sushi rice. The Chicken Katsu Donburi Rice is comforting and deeply satisfying, while the Baoji Style Sizzled Chilli Chicken is fiery, aromatic, and perfectly balanced.

The Purple Chicken Bao remains one of our absolute favourites—soft, pillowy, and bursting with flavour. The Chicken and Scallop Siu, Crab Meat Spicy Dumplings, and Sichuan Tiger Prawns are standout dishes that elevate the experience further. The Miso Ramen Bowl (chicken) and Pad Thai Noodles are soulful and generous, while the Japanese Tebasaki Chicken is addictive. The New Zealand Lamb Chops, whether in black pepper sauce or mixed berry teriyaki glaze, are succulent and refined.

One dish that truly steals the show is the banana-wrapped fish with sticky rice—the gravy, the fragrant rice, and the perfectly steamed fish wrapped in banana leaf come together in a spectacular, unforgettable combination.

They also boast a commendable selection of sashimi and nigiri, along with excellent soups and salads that complement the meal beautifully.

What truly completes the experience is the warm, humble hospitality of the staff. It has been many years of being regulars here, and Baoji remains our favourite monthly ritual. This isn’t just dining—it’s a celebration of flavours, craftsmanship, and heartfelt service.

It was my first time trying Pan Asian cuisine and let's say I was beyond happy with my experience at Yazu. First off, the ambience is great, it's spacious, lots of seating, great lighting and vibe, with a beautiful bar. Secondly, the service was amazing, the food was served pretty quickly after the order was placed and the staff was very meticulous and attentive.

Now, the food. We started off with their Crispy Chicken Chen Fueng, which was just sooo flavourful, it was both crispy and soft and the portion size was good. Next we had the Siracha Chicken Dimsum, which were so appetizing to look at and they were so perfectly steamed, they outright melted in your mouth. After that, we had the Spicy Tuna Roll Sushi, highly recommended for non vegetarians. Then we had the Shoyu Ramen Bowl, it was good and it had a lot of Shiitake Mushroom so if that's not something you enjoy, you can avoid ordering that. Next we had the Sake Norwegian Salmon Sashimi, it came with a radish salad. And lastly we had the Chicken Donburi in Teriyaki Sauce, it was sweet and tasty, with sticky rice, thoroughly enjoyed it but be cautious of it's quantity while ordering.

Overall, I'd definitely recommend Yazu to be the place you go to try authentic asian food. There was also a buffet available which had everything starting from Soups, Salads, Sushi, Dimsum, Main Course, Dessert, etc. We didn't try it but it looked great and definitely on our list next time if it's there.

They also offer Gold and Platinum meal packages with options including soups, dim sums, appetizers, mains, desserts, mocktails, and even alcohol packages with beer, wine, whiskey, and gin selections. However, we preferred ordering dishes individually.

Being vegetarians, we explored their veg menu:

Rating: 4/5

They also have Korean stone pots, cocktails, and a good dessert variety which we couldn’t try this time. Service was smooth, valet parking was conveniently arranged, and the staff was polite and attentive.

The pricing is definitely on the higher side, but considering the location, ambience, and authentic flavors, it feels justified if you enjoy premium dining experiences and want to try something different.

featured_reviews.review_text: To begin with, this lockdown period has been a difficult one for me and I'm sure for a lot peeps out there too. We knew Chinese food was the ideal comfort food for the family and my God were we right. We took a chance with WokHong Andheri and I now order from here religiously twice a week. My favourites are the Kung Pao Chicken,  Crispy Fried Chicken, Drums of Heaven, Hong's Dynamite Chicken for starters, Triple Schezwan Fried Rice, Soya Chilly Fried Rice, Burnt Garlic Noodles, Malaysian Curry Chicken with Rice, Oyster Chicken Gravy, Chicken in Black Bean Sauce, Prawns Manchurian, Salt N Pepper Fish for mains and many more mouth watering items I intend to explore over time. featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have fond memories of Firebowl from my college days, and when I was in Andheri recently, I decided to visit with my colleagues. The decor has seen a small but noticeable improvement with the addition of a fish tank, which gives the place a fresh look. Firebowl mainly serves Chinese food, and on this visit, we chose to have Indo-Chinese dishes.

We started with Veg Dumplings, which were decent. The outer layer could have been softer, but the filling was good, and the accompanying sauce complemented them well. They also serve fried noodles with Schezwan chutney, similar to what you find at street food stalls, and it was a good way to get started with the meal.

For the starters, we tried Hunan-Style Paneer Dry. The gravy and preparation were nice. However, the paneer was a bit chewy and did not feel as soft and of a good quality as one would expect. For the main course, we had Veg Burnt Chili Rice. The rice was delicious, spicy, and flavorful enough to not need any additional sauce or gravy.

Overall, it was a decent visit. The service was friendly, though the food took a little longer than expected to arrive. The seating is comfortable, but the glasses could have been cleaner.

If you are around this area and in the mood for Indo-Chinese food, Firebowl is worth a visit. The paneer dishes are okay, but the texture might not be for everyone.

Ratings:
Quality – 3.5/5
Quantity – 4/5
Service – 3.5/5
Price – ₹1150 for 5 people

featured_reviews.name: imran badami
featured_reviews.review_text:
Eating out on weekends is my favourite activities, especially trying out new restaurants. I would like to talk abt Chimichurri which i enjoyed.

Very spacious, I enjoyed the ambience of the restaurant. The tinted glasses added to the vibe of the place. As soon as u enter u will notice a fully stocked bar, which sets up the tone. We were offered the best seats in the house which always gives me a high. Missed an instagramable corner to capture a perfect moment at Chimichurri .

The staff were friendly and attentive. They made special efforts to ensure that we were comfortable throughout our meal. Browine points to Shital for excellent service and recommendations.

The feel-good music added to the atmosphere of the restaurant. The songs were peppy and made us sway to its rhythm.

What we ate

Chimichurri chicken dumplings - the dumplings were delicious. Flavourful fillings with a thin skin.

Tempura shrimp - crispy, crunchy, yummy served with wasabi and chilly garlic dipping sauce.

Chimichurri Ramen with noodles - Umami flavours. This was more soupy, if the portion of the noodles would be more then this would become saucy - an unbeatable dish.

Chu cha prawns - hot crispy prawns tossed in chillies and egg whites along with yummy spices seasoning. This was surely a wok to remember.

Mango tres leches - this was served complimentry to us. The tres leches was moist with 3 different types of milk, creamy and had mango written all over it. The portion size was huge yet we managed to polish it off in seconds.

Spiced jamun lemonade - fizzy jamun and chilly, a match made in heaven.

Mango basil smootie - this was good, could have been better. Missed the overpowering flavors of mango and basil both. This had vanilla written all over it. Served in a fancy glass could be more presentable with garnishing.

At Chimichurri, you will not want a perfect lunch date to end in a hurri.

featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Global Fusion at Versova for lunch and had a delightful experience. This place is a paradise for foodies—especially if you’re someone with a big appetite or a love for non-vegetarian dishes. The spread is massive, offering more than 20 starters served right to your table, a wide-ranging buffet, a tempting dessert counter, and complimentary beverages, which add great value to the overall experience.

If you love sushi, this is definitely the place for you. They offer unlimited sushi with various options, and everything is freshly prepared and well-presented. The seafood selection is also impressive—with dishes featuring prawns, bhetki, and crab that are cooked to perfection. The prawn tempura and dumplings were personal favorites.

The ambiance is warm and spacious, ideal for group lunches, celebrations, or casual family meals. The staff was polite and attentive, ensuring a smooth dining experience.

Having dined earlier at the Worli branch, I personally felt the food quality and taste there were slightly better compared to the Versova outlet, especially in terms of seasoning and presentation. However, that doesn’t take away from the fact that Versova still offers great value and variety.

Overall, if you’re a non veg lover or someone who enjoys variety in a buffet, Global Fusion Versova is worth a visit. Great food, vibrant vibe, and plenty to indulge in!

featured_reviews.name: VIKRANT JADHAV
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently hosted our office party at Amazonia. While the venue and ambiance were good, there were a few aspects that did not meet our expectations.

The DJ/music was stopped around 9:30 PM, which felt quite early for a corporate party. We also requested a few Marathi songs, but were informed that they were not permitted. What made this more surprising was that music and DJ activities at the neighboring venue, Butterfly High, appeared to continue until around midnight. Future guests may want to clarify the DJ timings, music policy, and any restrictions before confirming their booking.

The food quality, especially some of the starters, could be improved. The fish fingers had a noticeable oily smell, and the chicken wings were not enjoyed by most members of our group. The cheese balls were the only starter that received consistently positive feedback from our team.

Overall, the venue has a nice atmosphere, but I would recommend clarifying the entertainment schedule and menu expectations beforehand to ensure a smoother experience.
